newsitem.title: USA: Competition for Serono drug continues.
newsitem.headline: Competition for Serono drug continues.

text.p: Serono Laboratories Inc said Wednesday that the U.S. Court of Appeals has stayed an injunction blocking the sale of Ferring Pharmaceuticals' Repronex, a generic version of Serono's Pergonal.

The appeals court decision Tuesday allows Repronex to remain on the market while the full legal process moves forward, Serono said. The Ares-Serono SA subsidiary pointed out the Court of Appeals has not yet decided whether U.S. Food and Drug Administration properly approved Repronex.
A preliminary injunction barring Repronex was issued July 26 by the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia.
The injunction was issued on the basis of "certain questions related to the safety of Repronex" and other issues. The drug was approved by the FDA in January 1997.
Serono alleged Ferring asked for the stay, in part, because of its fragile financial situation. The appeals court granted an emergency stay pending appeal and expedited hearing.
The court established an expedited briefing schedule for the appeals process, beginning September 19, with concluding briefs due on November 3.
Responding to the appeals court, Serono said it "is confident that the original district court decision barring the marketing of Repronex is correct and appropriate."
It described the District Court ruling in July as the first step in challenging the FDA decision to allow the marketing of Repronex as a generic product.
For a product to be approved as a generic in the U.S., it must demonstrate that it is "the same as" or "identical to" the pioneer product, its statement noted.

It said "the record in this case clearly shows that two chemistry reviews by FDA's own scientists concluded Pergonal and Repronex are not 'the same' or 'identical' drugs. In addition, Serono has submitted its own data demonstrating how the two products differ in both active and inactive ingredients. Despite these differences, which prevent approval as a generic, the record shows that Ferring has not submitted any clinical trial data for the approval of its menotropins product."
